title: Email Not Working
cardText: Diagnose email sending, receiving, sign-in, synchronisation and attachment problems.
Separate mailbox or provider faults from email application and device problems.
Includes official setup and troubleshooting links for Outlook, Thunderbird, Apple Mail and other email clients.
text: This guide covers email problems across desktop applications, mobile devices and webmail.
Start by identifying the symptom and whether the mailbox works through the provider's webmail service.
Use generic checks for account access, delivery, storage, synchronisation and server configuration.
Follow the linked manufacturer instructions for client-specific settings and repair procedures.
Preserve local mail data before removing accounts, rebuilding profiles or changing POP configurations.

identifyEmailProblem.title: Identify the email problem
body: Determine whether the problem affects sending or receiving messages, or involves sign-in and synchronisation.
Record any error message, server response or authentication warning.
Note whether the issue affects one account, multiple accounts or several devices.
For missing emails, check whether messages are absent from webmail or only from the email application.

testWebmail.title: Compare the email client with webmail
body: Access the mailbox through the email provider's official webmail service, where available.
Check whether recent messages appear and whether a simple test message can be sent.
Compare this with the behaviour in the affected email application.
If webmail works but the application fails, investigate client configuration, authentication and synchronisation.
If webmail also fails, investigate the account, provider or mail delivery system.
For accounts without webmail, compare against another configured device or use the provider's diagnostic tools.

checkProviderStatus.title: Check email provider availability
body: Check the email provider's official service status or support information.
Determine whether the issue affects mail delivery, authentication or the webmail service.
For business email, check the organisation's service health dashboard or mail administrator.
Check whether other accounts hosted by the same provider are affected.
If a confirmed service outage explains the problem, avoid unnecessary local account changes.
If the provider is functioning normally, continue with account diagnostics.

waitForProvider.title: Email provider outage identified
body: The provider has confirmed a service disruption affecting the mailbox.
Monitor the provider's status updates for the affected service.
Avoid changing working passwords or account configurations during an outage.
Retest webmail and the email application once service is restored.

checkAccountCredentials.title: Check account authentication
body: Review the exact authentication error reported by the provider.
Determine whether the account is locked, its password was changed or additional verification is required.
Check whether multifactor authentication or a provider-specific app password is involved.
Modern Microsoft and Google accounts generally use supported interactive sign-in or OAuth authentication in compatible clients.
Do not assume that an ordinary account password will work with every older POP or IMAP application.
If account recovery is necessary, use the provider's official recovery process.

link.name: Microsoft: Outlook account setup and password help
link.description: Guidance for account authentication, app passwords and adding supported email accounts.

link.name: Google Account Recovery
link.description: Official recovery service for Gmail and Google account sign-in failures.

resetEmailPassword.title: Recover email account access
body: The email provider is rejecting access or requires additional account verification.
Use its official account recovery or password reset procedure.
For organisation-managed accounts, contact the appropriate administrator.
Complete required multifactor authentication or account security checks.
After restoring access, update affected email clients using the provider's supported authentication method.
Avoid repeated sign-in attempts that may trigger additional account lockouts.

link.description: Official Gmail and Google account recovery process.

checkMailboxStorage.title: Check mailbox storage and account restrictions
body: Inspect mailbox storage usage in the provider's account settings.
Check whether the account has reached a storage or sending quota.
Look for account restrictions, suspicious activity warnings or licensing problems.
A full mailbox may prevent delivery or affect outgoing mail depending on the provider.
If storage and account status are normal, investigate message filtering and delivery.

freeMailboxStorage.title: Resolve mailbox quota or account limits
body: Identify the specific mailbox storage or sending restriction.
Remove unnecessary messages and large attachments when appropriate.
Review Deleted Items, Junk and other folders that may contribute to mailbox usage.
For business mailboxes, check retention policies and available storage licensing before deleting data.
Resolve any account suspension or sending restriction through the provider.
Retest mail delivery after the restriction is cleared.

checkSpamAndRules.title: Check mail filtering and folder rules
body: Search the mailbox for a message that appears to be missing.
Check Junk, Spam, Deleted Items, Archive, quarantine and other folders.
Review inbox rules, filters, forwarding settings and blocked senders.
For managed email, check whether a server-side security filter quarantined the message.
If an unexpected forwarding rule or filter appears, consider whether the account has been compromised.
If no missing message is found, continue with sending and receiving diagnostics.

mailRuleIssue.title: Mail filtering or folder problem identified
body: The missing email was found in another folder or affected by a mail rule.
Correct the relevant filter, rule, blocked sender or quarantine setting.
Review unexpected forwarding rules for possible unauthorised changes.
Restore or move messages as appropriate.
Retest delivery with the original sender.

checkSendOrReceive.title: Determine which mail direction is failing
body: Test sending a simple email to another accessible address.
Send a separate message from that address back to the affected mailbox.
Check whether outgoing messages are accepted and incoming messages arrive.
Record any nondelivery report or server error returned.
If both sending and receiving fail, account authentication, provider or server configuration may be involved.
Choose the direction with the clearest failure; the other can be tested afterwards.

checkIncomingMail.title: Diagnose incoming mail delivery
body: Send a test message from an independent email account.
Check whether the message reaches the provider's webmail mailbox.
If it reaches webmail but not the client, investigate synchronisation and folder settings.
If it never reaches the provider, check for a sender nondelivery report.
For custom-domain email, investigate MX records, mailbox routing, spam filtering and server-side restrictions.
Do not change the email client's incoming server settings if the message has not reached the provider.

incomingServerIssue.title: Incoming mail delivery problem
body: The test message is not reaching the mailbox on the provider's server.
Check any nondelivery report for a delivery error or rejection reason.
Investigate mailbox quotas, blocked senders, filtering and account restrictions.
For custom domains, verify MX records and mail hosting configuration.
For organisation-managed accounts, inspect available mail-flow or message-trace logs.
Contact the mail hosting provider or domain administrator when server-side troubleshooting is required.

checkOutgoingMail.title: Diagnose outgoing mail
body: Send a plain-text test email without attachments to a known-working external address.
Check whether the email leaves the Outbox and appears in Sent Items.
Record any SMTP rejection, authentication failure or nondelivery message.
If plain mail sends but the original message does not, inspect attachment size, blocked file types and recipient details.
If even a basic message fails, investigate the Outbox and outgoing server configuration.

attachmentOrRecipientIssue.title: Message, attachment or recipient problem likely
body: A plain test message sends successfully.
Compare the failing message with the working test.
Check recipient addresses, attachment size, file type and provider sending limits.
For large attachments, use an approved cloud-sharing method where appropriate.
Review any rejection or nondelivery report for the exact reason.
Retest after correcting the affected message.

checkOutbox.title: Check outgoing message queue
body: Inspect the email client's Outbox or pending-send folder.
Check whether a failed message remains queued.
Look for an offline mode, paused synchronisation or repeated authentication errors.
Move a stuck message to Drafts or preserve a copy before deleting it.
Try sending a new small test message.
If the message remains queued, investigate the account's outgoing server configuration.

clearOutbox.title: Resolve stuck outgoing messages
body: Preserve any unsent message content before removing it from the Outbox.
Remove or move the stuck message and reconnect the client if it was offline.
Check whether another message or attachment is causing repeated failures.
Retry with a simple outgoing test message.
If sending still fails, investigate SMTP authentication and server settings.

checkSmtpSettings.title: Check outgoing server configuration
body: Determine whether the account is using SMTP or a provider-managed Exchange or API connection.
For manually configured SMTP accounts, compare the outgoing server hostname, port, encryption and authentication settings with the provider's instructions.
Check whether SMTP authentication is enabled when required.
Use the provider's current TLS and authentication requirements rather than assuming that older saved settings remain valid.
Common submission ports include 587 with STARTTLS and 465 with implicit TLS, but the provider's supported settings take precedence.
For modern Microsoft or Google accounts, prefer the supported account sign-in method rather than forcing basic password authentication.
If the settings match the provider's recommendations, investigate network or security software interference.

fixSmtpSettings.title: Correct outgoing mail server settings
body: Use the email provider's current outgoing server settings.
Correct the SMTP hostname, supported port, encryption and authentication configuration.
Check the account username and supported sign-in method.
Do not disable encryption to work around an authentication failure.
Save the changes and send a small test message.
If the client still cannot send, investigate local network and security restrictions.

checkLoginProblem.title: Identify authentication or synchronisation failure
body: Determine whether the client repeatedly prompts for credentials, rejects sign-in or simply stops synchronising.
Record the exact error message and any provider authentication code.
Check whether the account requires multifactor verification, a supported OAuth sign-in or administrator approval.
If the account cannot authenticate through the provider's website, investigate account recovery.
If authentication works elsewhere but the client does not update, investigate the email application.

checkMailAppIssue.title: Check whether the email application is responsible
body: Compare the affected client with webmail or another working device.
Check whether the issue affects one mailbox, all accounts in the app or only particular folders.
Inspect offline status, sync errors and account authentication warnings.
Check that the mail client supports the account provider's current authentication requirements.
If webmail works and the failure is confined to one client, continue with application troubleshooting.
If the account fails across multiple devices and webmail, investigate the provider or account instead.

checkClientSync.title: Check mail application synchronisation
body: Check whether the client is offline, paused or displaying a sync error.
Use the application's supported Send/Receive or Sync operation.
Check whether messages appear in the expected folder and whether a folder filter is hiding them.
Compare the account's folder contents with webmail.
Check whether the app is up to date and supported by the email provider.
If synchronisation remains broken, investigate saved account credentials and configuration.

link.name: Microsoft: Sync Mail in New and Classic Outlook
link.description: Official Send/Receive and Sync instructions for both Outlook applications.

link.name: Mozilla: Thunderbird Support
link.description: Thunderbird help articles covering synchronisation and account configuration.

checkSavedPassword.title: Check saved account authentication
body: Check whether the email account password or security settings changed recently.
If the application repeatedly prompts for a password, review any reported authentication error.
Reauthenticate through the provider's supported sign-in screen where available.
For legacy or manually configured accounts, check whether an app-specific password is required and supported.
For managed accounts, confirm that the application is approved by the organisation's security policies.
Avoid repeatedly deleting saved credentials without identifying which account or connection is failing.
If reauthentication does not resolve the problem, review the client's account configuration.

link.name: Microsoft: Outlook Email Setup and Authentication
link.description: Guidance for adding email accounts and resolving supported password or app-password problems.

checkClientSettings.title: Review email client settings and setup instructions
body: Identify the email application and the account provider.
Check whether the account uses Exchange, IMAP or POP, or another supported connection type.
Use the provider's automatic setup method when available.
For manual IMAP or POP accounts, compare incoming and outgoing server details with the provider's current documentation.
Do not assume settings from one email client apply to another.
The links below provide client-specific setup and troubleshooting instructions for new Outlook, classic Outlook, Thunderbird and Apple Mail.
If the configuration is correct but the client still fails, investigate repair or account recreation options.

link.description: Official account setup and management instructions for new Outlook.

link.description: Official instructions for configuring and troubleshooting email accounts in classic Outlook.

checkAccountData.title: Check for locally stored mail before repairs
body: Before removing an account or rebuilding a profile, identify how its email is stored.
IMAP and Exchange accounts generally synchronise mailbox data with a server, although locally stored or exported content may not be synchronised.
POP accounts may contain messages downloaded only to the local computer.
Check for local folders, archives, Outlook PST files and Thunderbird local mail data where relevant.
Back up important locally stored messages, contacts, calendars and account settings.
Confirm that the account can be accessed through webmail or another working device before removing its configuration.
If the data is protected and recoverable, proceed with an appropriate client repair.

preserveLocalMail.title: Preserve local email data before continuing
body: The email application may contain messages or data not stored on the provider's server.
Back up relevant mail archives, locally stored messages, contacts and calendars.
Do not remove a POP account or delete an Outlook or Thunderbird profile until the important data is protected.
Use the application's export or backup procedure where appropriate.
Once the backup has been verified, continue with client repair or account recreation.

repairMailClient.title: Repair the email client or account configuration
body: Use the email application's supported account repair or profile troubleshooting tools.
For classic Outlook, the account Repair option may be available, depending on account type.
For new Outlook, review the account management and sign-in settings.
For Thunderbird, review account settings and available troubleshooting procedures before rebuilding the profile.
Avoid clearing application data, removing profiles or deleting cache folders without checking their effect on locally stored messages.
After applying a supported repair, verify sending, receiving and folder synchronisation.

removeAndReaddAccount.title: Recreate the email account configuration
body: Only proceed after verifying mailbox access and protecting important local data.
Record the account address, connection type and any required server settings.
Use the email client's supported account removal and setup procedure.
Re-add the account using automatic configuration where available.
For manual configurations, use the provider's current IMAP, POP, SMTP and authentication requirements.
Allow time for folders and messages to resynchronise.
Verify sending, receiving, contacts and calendar access as applicable.
If the account remains broken, check for network or security software interference.

link.name: Mozilla: Thunderbird Account Configuration

checkSecuritySoftware.title: Check VPN, firewall and security interference
body: Review security software, VPN and firewall logs for blocked email connections.
Check whether the failure occurs only on a particular network or while connected to a VPN.
For manually configured accounts, confirm that the required server ports are permitted.
Check whether security software is interfering with encrypted mail connections or authentication.
Do not permanently disable endpoint protection to make email work.
For organisation-managed devices, consult the administrator before changing firewall or security policies.

securitySoftwareIssue.title: Correct the confirmed network or security issue
body: Identify the VPN, firewall or security product responsible for blocking mail access.
Review the product's official configuration and troubleshooting instructions.
Correct the relevant rule, certificate handling or network setting.
Do not leave security protection disabled.
Retest the affected account after the correction.

finalEmailEscalation.title: Further email diagnostics required
body: The problem persists after checking account access, webmail, delivery, client settings and local security software.
Record the email provider, application, version, account type and exact error messages.
For hosted mailboxes, investigate account restrictions, authentication policies and server-side logs.
For custom domains, check mail routing and DNS records where relevant.
For Microsoft 365 or other managed email, inspect available message trace and service health information.
If the problem affects one email client only, review its profile, data files and application-specific diagnostics.
Preserve local mail data before undertaking destructive repairs.
Contact the mail hosting provider, application vendor or responsible administrator with the troubleshooting results.
